name: Lunar-17 (level-1 Mystic pregen, design doc §19 Pure RAW SF2E Validation — real Paizo Adventure Pregen, NOT one of the six real campaign kids)
notes: Every combat number here is real, derived SF2E math (tools/character-builder/derive.mjs + build-combat-pregen.mjs), cross-checked against her own raw pack data (gamesystems/sf2e/packs/paizo-pregens) — see test/character-builder/build-combat-pregen.test.mjs and design/scale-and-chassis.md §19/§21. Transfer Vitality's healing amount (10, minimum 1) is hand-transcribed from real rule prose since no structured field exists for it — see build-combat-pregen.mjs's own citation. GH #55: usesRemaining/usesPerEncounter (2) are hand-authored here, NOT derived — the real limit isn't a per-day slot count but the Mystic's own 'vitality network' resource pool (Vitality Network feat, Player Core: capacity 6+4/level = 10 at level 1, regenerating 4 HP at the start of each of the caster's turns in combat — more if master/legendary in spell DC, refilling fully on Refocus), a mechanic this single-encounter simulator doesn't simulate HP-for-HP. At level 1 the pool's capacity exactly equals one use's cost (10=10), so a flat 2-per-encounter cap ('usable once at full charge, once more after a few turns' partial regen') is the same approximation already shipped for the level-12 Frame-scale Mystic (data/combatants.mjs's makeMysticFrame, pool 54 / cost 30 / same regen rate — also capped at 2 for the identical reason). The caster's own currentHP is correctly UNTOUCHED by this ability — Transfer Vitality draws from the network, never the caster's own HP total, confirmed directly against the real extracted rule text (not assumed from the ability's name). Her Incendiary Grenade (Commercial) is real but NOT wired as a usable action: its raw description reads "Activate 1 Area Fire ... (@Template[burst|distance:5])" — a 5ft-burst AREA effect, not a single-target attack, structurally identical to Frag Grenade/Electromag Grenade (already excluded for other pregens for the same reason). personnel-engine's saveAttack action is single-target only; wiring a burst weapon through it would have hit exactly one creature with none of the real friendly-fire risk an area weapon actually carries, and was in fact caught doing exactly that (see design doc §21's grenade-modeling correction).
